useCase.name: Record a movement as a voucher, approved by a chain that matches its size, and paid separately
useCase.featureRef: 4.19 Accounting vouchers for money in and out

intent.name: finance.voucher.create
intent.summary: Enter a movement as a voucher — both sides in one entry, with what the money was for. One step, and it posts nothing.
routesHere: enter a payment voucher for the electricity bill, 18,000

routesHere.text: bijli ka bill ka voucher bana do — 18,000
routesHere.gloss: make a voucher for the electricity bill — 18,000

routesHere.text: cash bank mein jama karwaya, contra voucher banao
routesHere.gloss: cash was deposited into the bank, make a contra voucher

routesHere: raise a receipt voucher for the canteen rent

routesElsewhere.note: Creating and authorising are separate hands (BR-10).

request.text: paisa de diya hai, record kar do
request.gloss: the money has been paid, record it

routesElsewhere.note: Approving a payment and making it are separate acts (BR-8).
A fee receipt has its own route; this is for movements that do not.
A posted voucher is never edited or deleted. A correction is a further voucher, so the ledger reads as a history (BR-11).

steps.note: One step. Both sides of the movement are captured in a single entry (BR-1), and the voucher reaches the ledger only on final approval — a draft posts nothing (BR-5).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Matching debit and credit accounts, unbalanced sides, a closed period and a missing chart of accounts are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors. A budget line the voucher would exceed is flagged and pushed up a level, never blocked (BR-9).
plan.atomicity: One write: the voucher at Draft with both its sides, and the audit entry. Nothing reaches the ledger — a draft or a voucher awaiting approval posts nothing (BR-5). Where a budget line applies, its remaining balance is checked and shown now, so an overspend is visible before submission rather than after (BR-9).

operations.name: finance.voucher.create
operations.idempotencyKey: voucher_type + amount + debit_account_id + credit_account_id + voucher_date + description, so a repeat does not create a second voucher for the same movement
operations.purpose: Create a draft voucher capturing both sides of a movement, with its accounts, date, amount and description.

parameters.name: voucher_type
parameters.type: enum: Payment voucher | Receipt voucher | Journal voucher | Contra voucher
parameters.notes: What kind of movement this is. Read from what the actor stated.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.notes: Greater than zero. It decides which approval the voucher needs (BR-3), so a figure a planner supplied would also choose the approval chain.

parameters.name: debit_account_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No such account in the chart of accounts.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with code and name.

parameters.notes: From the chart of accounts. Must differ from the credit account (BR-6, E1).

parameters.name: credit_account_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No such account in the chart of accounts.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with code and name.

parameters.notes: From the chart of accounts. Must differ from the debit account.

parameters.name: voucher_date
parameters.notes: When the movement occurred. Not in the future, and within an open period — a movement cannot be posted into a closed one (BR-13, E3).

parameters.name: description
parameters.notes: 20 to 500 characters. What the money was for, in terms a reader can follow. The actor's own words.

parameters.name: payee
parameters.notes: Who the money is paid to. Required in substance for a payment voucher.

parameters.name: supporting_document_id
parameters.notes: The bill, quotation or receipt behind the movement, uploaded on the screen. A payment with no bill behind it is the thing an auditor asks about (BR-12).

parameters.name: budget_line_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with account or department and remaining balance.

parameters.notes: The budget line this spends against, where one exists. Its remaining balance is shown before submission (BR-9).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The voucher as drafted, and what it will need.

fields.name: approval_required
fields.description: Derived from the amount and the two thresholds. Never chosen (BR-3).

fields.name: budget_remaining
fields.description: What is left on the line, shown before submission so an overspend is visible (BR-9).

fields.name: exceeds_budget
fields.description: True where it would take the line over. Flagged and pushed to the next approval level up, never blocked (BR-9).

fields.name: has_supporting_document
fields.description: False is worth reporting — a payment with no bill behind it is what an auditor asks about (BR-12).

errors.meaning: The debit and credit accounts are the same.
The two sides do not total the same.
errors.note: A voucher that does not balance is not posted (BR-6).

errors.meaning: The voucher date falls in a closed period.
errors.note: A movement cannot be posted into a closed one (BR-13). Never move the date to an open period to get past this — the date is when the movement occurred.

planningRules.rule: Never supply the amount. It decides which approval chain the voucher needs (BR-3), so a figure a planner chose also chooses who gets to authorise it.
Never choose the accounts. Which account is debited and which credited is what the entry means, and a plausible-looking pair puts real money in the wrong place in the books.
Never move the voucher date to get past a closed period. The date is when the movement occurred (BR-13), and redating it to an open period records the movement in the wrong month.

Report an over-budget line rather than treating it as a refusal. An excess is flagged and pushed to the next approval level up, never blocked (BR-9, BR-1 of UC-04-20) — blocking routine spending stalls the office, and the escalation is the deliberate middle ground.
Report when no supporting document is attached. A payment with no bill behind it is the thing an auditor asks about first (BR-12).
Never edit a posted voucher. A correction is a further voucher, so the ledger reads as a history (BR-11).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A draft is not deleted; it is submitted, approved, returned or left. Once posted, a voucher is never edited or deleted — a correction is a further voucher (BR-11). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

intent.name: finance.voucher.approve
intent.summary: Approve a voucher at the level its amount requires, posting it to the ledger and creating the payable. One step.

routesElsewhere.note: Approving a payment and making it are separate acts, so an approved but unpaid voucher is a visible liability (BR-8).
Both thresholds are set by the Principal, not the School Admin — a limit should not be settable by the person it constrains (BR-4, E7). No capability sets them; see OPEN-QUESTIONS.

steps.note: One step, and the level required is derived from the amount rather than chosen (BR-3). On final approval the voucher posts and a payable is created, because the school now owes the money (BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Approving above the acting user's threshold, and a ledger posting that fails, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the approval, the ledger posting on final approval, the payable and the audit entry together or not at all (E9). The voucher reaches the ledger only on final approval — an intermediate approval posts nothing (BR-5). Approval creates a payable, since the school now owes the money; the printed voucher is the authorisation to release it rather than a second record to key (BR-7). The money has **not** left — that is a separate act (BR-8).

operations.name: finance.voucher.approve
operations.idempotencyKey: voucher_id + the approving level, so a repeat does not record a second approval at the same level
operations.purpose: Record an approval at the acting user's level, posting the voucher and creating the payable once the chain is complete.

parameters.name: voucher_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No voucher matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with number, type, amount, payee and status.

parameters.notes: The voucher, resolved from how the actor named it — the voucher number, the payee and amount, or the description.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The approval, and where the voucher now stands.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Awaiting Principal, Approved, or Posted where the chain is complete.

fields.name: further_approval_required
fields.description: The next level, where the chain is not complete (BR-3).

fields.name: payable_created
fields.description: The payable raised, since the school now owes the money (BR-7).

fields.name: budget_consumed
fields.description: The line this now consumes, so a commitment is visible before the money leaves (UC-04-20 BR-5).

fields.name: paid
fields.description: Always false. Approving a payment and making it are separate acts (BR-8).

errors.meaning: Accounts attempted to approve a voucher above the lower threshold.
errors.note: Accounts cannot approve a voucher above the lower threshold, including one they created (BR-10).

errors.meaning: A School Admin attempted to approve above the higher threshold.

errors.note: Message: "The voucher could not be posted. Nothing has changed."

planningRules.rule: Never choose the approval level. It is derived from the amount and the two thresholds (BR-3), and a planner selecting one would be selecting who gets to authorise the money.
Never approve a voucher the acting user created where it is above the lower threshold. Creating and authorising are separate hands (BR-10).

Report that the money has not left. Approval creates a payable and the school now owes it (BR-7); making the payment is a separate act (BR-8), and an approved but unpaid voucher is a visible liability rather than a completed payment.
Report the next approval level where the chain is not complete. A voucher sitting at Awaiting Principal is not approved, and the supplier is not going to be paid until somebody notices.
Never chain the payment onto the approval. The printed voucher is the authorisation to release the money, not the release (BR-7, BR-8).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A posted voucher is never edited or deleted (BR-11). Where it was wrong, a further voucher corrects it, so the ledger reads as a history. An approved but unpaid voucher can be cancelled through the voucher lifecycle, but nothing here reverses a posting. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

intent.name: finance.voucher.pay
intent.summary: Record that an approved voucher has been paid, discharging the payable and posting the cash movement. One step.
routesHere: record the electricity voucher as paid, the transfer went today

routesHere.text: voucher ki payment record kar do
paisa de diya hai, voucher paid mark karo
routesHere.gloss: the money has been paid, mark the voucher paid

routesHere: mark this voucher paid with the transfer reference

routesElsewhere.note: A payment cannot be recorded against an unapproved voucher (E10).

steps.note: One step. It discharges the payable and posts the cash movement — approving a payment and making it are separate acts, which is why this exists at all (BR-8).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A payment against an unapproved voucher is enforced by the API and arrives as an error.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the payable discharged, the cash movement posted and the audit entry together or not at all. The approval entry stays as it was — this adds the second half of the story rather than amending the first (BR-11).

operations.name: finance.voucher.pay
operations.idempotencyKey: voucher_id, since a voucher is paid once and a repeat must not post the cash movement twice
operations.purpose: Record an approved voucher as paid, discharging the payable and posting the cash movement.

parameters.name: voucher_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No voucher matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with number, type, amount, payee and status.

parameters.notes: The voucher, resolved from how the actor named it — the voucher number, the payee and amount, or the description.

parameters.name: paid_on
parameters.notes: When the money actually left, recorded separately from approval (BR-8). Only where the request states it — a date defaulted to today misstates when the school's cash went.

parameters.name: payment_reference
parameters.notes: The cheque number or transfer reference, where the request supplies one.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: cash_movement_posted
fields.description: The ledger entry for the money leaving.

errors.meaning: The voucher has not been approved.
errors.note: Message: "This voucher has not been approved." Approving it is a separate act by somebody else (BR-8, BR-10).

planningRules.rule: Never default the paid date to today. It is when the money actually left, recorded separately from approval (BR-8), and the two differ whenever a cheque waits for collection.
Never chain an approval onto a payment. E10 is BR-10 working — creating, authorising and paying are three hands, and approving a voucher to make a payment record succeed removes the control entirely.
Never record a payment before the money has gone. It discharges the payable and posts the cash movement, and a payable discharged against a transfer that never left overstates the school's cash.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A posted cash movement is never edited or deleted (BR-11). Where the payment was recorded wrongly, a further voucher corrects it. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

operations.name: finance.voucher.return
operations.purpose: Send a voucher back to Accounts with the reason it was not approved.

parameters.name: voucher_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No voucher matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with number, type, amount, payee and status.

parameters.notes: The voucher, resolved from how the actor named it — the voucher number, the payee and amount, or the description.

parameters.name: return_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Required (E8) — Accounts have to know what to correct. The approver's own words.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

errors.meaning: A voucher was returned with no reason.
errors.note: Message: "Give a reason so Accounts know what to correct." Ask; never compose one.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the return reason. Accounts have to know whether the accounts, the amount, the date, the description or the missing bill is the problem (E8).

Never adjust the voucher on the approver's behalf. Changing an account or an amount is Accounts' work in their own session — and the amount decides the approval chain (BR-3), so changing it changes who approves.
Report that nothing has posted and nobody has been paid. A returned voucher is a supplier still waiting.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A return is not undone. Accounts correct the voucher and submit it again, which is a fresh approval chain from the level its amount requires.
